source_text: Quid igitur actum est? Videlicet tam certum esse traducem non esse peccati ut, etiamsi doceres propter Adae peccatum filios puniri, constaret tamen innasci peccata non posse nec crimen ire cum semine, quando non hoc in omni fecunditate esse faterere; ac per hoc, etsi traderentur personis vitia, non tamen conceptibus miscerentur. Nunc au tem cum inter me et te conveniat parentum peccatum ad filios nisi vitio et reatu generationis non potuisse transire, rationi autem, exemplis legique convenerit generationis statum nullo pacto potuisse vitiari, quod ex tua etiam concessione firmatur, qui dicis nullorum parentum peccata praeter duorum ad liberos permeare, invictissime confectum est nec fecunditatem primorum hominum a diabolo fuisse corruptam nec nasci ullum posse peccatum.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore has been done? Namely that it is so certain there is not a vine-layer of sin that, even if you taught sons are punished on account of Adam's sin, it would nevertheless stand that sins cannot be inborn nor crime go with seed, when you would confess this is not in every fecundity; and through this, even if vices were handed to persons, they would nevertheless not be mixed into conceptions. Now however when between me and you it is agreed that a parent's sin could not have passed to sons except by vice and guilt of generation, but it has agreed with reason, examples, and the law that the status of generation could by no pact have been vitiated, which is also confirmed from your concession, who say that the sins of no parents besides two permeate to children, it has been most unconquerably accomplished that neither was the fecundity of the first humans corrupted by the devil nor can any sin be born.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: What, then, have we established? That the nonexistence of inherited sin is so certain that, even if you showed children punished for Adam’s sin, it would still be established that sins cannot be inborn and guilt cannot travel with reproductive seed, since you would admit that this does not happen in all reproduction. Consequently, even if vices were handed on to persons, they would not be mixed into conception.

But as it stands, you and I agree that a parent’s sin could not pass to children except through corruption and guilt in generation itself. Reason, examples, and the law agree that the condition of generation cannot possibly have been corrupted. Your own concession confirms this, for you say that no parents’ sins except those of two people pass to their children. It has therefore been established beyond defeat that the devil neither corrupted the first humans’ reproductive power nor made any sin capable of being born.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
